why: Moves are data, played by the renderer over a plate’s published slots; see engine/motion.js for each move’s per-frame function. No move fades (rule 2). Every loop is seamless: frame 12 is frame 0.

moves.appliesTo: a plot-area with a linePath (anchor.box, and anchor.also for small-multiple panels, all drawn on together)
moves.how: clip the data layer to reveal(outset(anchor.box, anchor.bleed), t, "left-linear"); the accent point appears on the last frame. Only the line moves: a figure counting up beside it is the count-up move, cued separately.

moves.appliesTo: plates with bar or stacked columns (anchor.columns, oldest first)
moves.how: column i is clipped to reveal(column.box, E.out(stagger(f, i, frames)), "bottom"), so each starts one frame after the one before; the accented column, if the data names one, goes last. The move lasts frames + columns - 1 frames.

moves.appliesTo: a slot with underline, or the quote slots
moves.how: a rect at TIMINGS.highlight under the line: anchor.lines[n-1] where n is the number of lines the copy sets, or anchor.box when there are no lines; width = reveal(line, t, "left").w x 0.8

moves.appliesTo: the figure slot anchorFor() names; the "this one" beat

moves.appliesTo: paper plates; the push in on a footnote
moves.how: viewBox = zoomBox(canvas, anchor.box, t, 60): the slot as published, padding 60

moves.appliesTo: rooms whose rooms[id].flicker or .lamp is not empty
moves.how: the shapes in rooms[id].flicker take their shade tone where SCREEN_PULSE[f]; rooms[id].lamp where LAMP_FLICKER[f]. Window and door panes and the daylight they cast (rooms[id].panes, .daylight) never flicker.

moves.appliesTo: rooms with a pane of kind "window"; December, with the Christmas set
moves.how: snow(pane.box, f) as paper-role squares of side r, painted straight after the pane shape (pane.shape), so every later shape (frame bars, sill, tree, him) paints over the flakes

moves.appliesTo: rooms with a pane of kind "window"; a gloomy episode
moves.how: RAIN(pane.box, f) as short glow-shade strokes, painted straight after the pane shape, like the snow
bulb b takes twinkleInk(b.phase, f): one ink step every 4 frames

tick-over.why: the old number is on screen for a quarter second so it is read, turns over by 0.75 s, and the new one holds the remaining 1.25 s of the two-second bumper. Frames are 0-based: frame 3 is the fourth frame.

source-tag.rule: 16:9: left edge at x 96 (the 5% safe margin), bottom edge 24 above the lower of the safe bottom (1026) and the plate’s caption. 9:16: centred, bottom edge 24 above the lower of the shorts safe line (1560) and the caption. Over a plate, use anchors.plates[key]["slide-in"], which applies this rule to that plate’s own slots and says whether the spot is clear. Where it says clear: false, do not lay the tag over that plate: put it on the next room or host shot, or speak the source.

highlight.why: the same rect the data layer draws for a slot that publishes underline: y = box bottom + 2, height 5, width 0.8 of the box

line-draw.why: the clip is the plot box grown by 14 on every side, so the line’s half-weight and the end points are not cut; nothing else on the plate moves with it

anchors.why: Where each move lands on each plate, READ from its published slots by motion.anchorFor(); null = the plate has nothing for that move, skip it. Never placed by eye. Boxes are in the plate’s canvas units.
